Proposed Charter Amendment City of Bedford Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Section 13.05 of the Charter of the City of Bedford Heights be amended to permit the Director of Finance's bond requirement to be satisfied by one or more insurance or risk-management policies or programs designed to protect the City against loss caused by dishonest acts, theft, or failure to faithfully perform official duties, including, without limitation, a Government Entity Crime Policy with a Faithful Performance of Duty endorsement, or any successor or substantially equivalent form of coverage maintained by the City, in an amount not less than that otherwise required for the bond, so long as such policy is maintained, in lieu of a separate surety bond?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Bedford Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Section 8.02 of the Charter of the City of Bedford Heights be amended to provide that the Director of Law shall be appointed by the Mayor rather than the Council, and shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Berea A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Item 1 of the Charter of the City of Berea be amended by expanding the terms for all members of Council and the President of Council from two (2) to four (4) year terms, starting for the regular municipal election to take place in 2027?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Berea A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XIII, Item 2 of the Charter of the City of Berea be amended to change the deadline for candidates submitting nominating petitions for municipal elective office of the City of Berea from not less than sixty (60) days to not less than ninety (90) days prior to the date of the primary election for such offices?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article III, Section 1(b), of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to provide that no person shall hold the office of councilperson for more than three (3) consecutive four (4) year terms or twelve (12) consecutive years; and that terms served prior to the effective date of this amendment shall not be counted?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Section 1 of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to provide that no person shall hold office of Mayor for more than three (3) consecutive 4 year terms or twelve (12) consecutive years unless one (1) full term or more had elapsed since that person last held the office of Mayor; and that terms served prior to the effective date of this amendment shall not be counted?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to add Section 4(d) to provide that the Mayor shall have the authority to enter into contracts on behalf of the City without prior Council approval as required pursuant to Article III, Section 7 of the Charter when the value of the contract is $25,000 or less, provided sufficient funds have otherwise been appropriated by council; and that the $25,000 threshold shall increase annually at a rate of 3% beginning January 1, 2028?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to add Section 4(e) to provide that the Mayor shall have the authority to make purchases on behalf of the City without prior Council approval when the value of purchase is $25,000 or less, provided sufficient funds have otherwise been appropriated by council; and that the $25,000 threshold shall increase annually at a rate of 3% beginning January 1, 2028?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article V, Section 5 of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to add Section 5(c) to provide that the City of Broadview Heights shall maintain two fire stations within the City, with each fire station having at least one fire truck and one EMS vehicle?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XI, of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to add Section 4 to provide that municipal tax levies can only be placed on the ballot for municipal elections held in November of any calendar year?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Broadview Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XIV, Section 8 of the Charter of the City of Broadview Heights be amended to add Section 8(d) to provide that under reprinting(s) of the Charter, any gender-specific terms shall be changed to gender neutral terms?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Brook Park A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Section 4.04 of the Charter of the City of Brook Park be amended to remove the requirement that any increase of over three percent (3%) in compensation for any elected City officials be approved by the electorate?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Brook Park A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XV, Section 15.01(c) of the Charter of the City of Brook Park be amended to provide that elected or appointed officials may serve as trustees for the Brook Park New Community Authority?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Garfield Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Sections 7 and 12 of the Charter of the City of Garfield Heights be amended to change the terms of all seven (7) members of Council from two (2) to four (4) years, beginning at the General Election held in November 2029; and to provide that Council shall elect one of its members President of Council at the first meeting in December following the General Election?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Independence A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article III, Section 3 of the Charter of the City of Independence be amended to provide that the Mayor shall attend all meetings of the Council, and remove the requirement that the Mayor preside over all meetings of the Council?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Independence A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Section 5(a) of the Charter of the City of Independence be amended to provide that, commencing January 1, 2027, the appointment of three (3) citizen members of the Planning Commission be changed from the Mayor to a majority of the members elected to Council?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Independence A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Section 5(c) of the Charter of the City of Independence be amended to provide that any zoning ordinances, regulations, or amendments passed by Council under this Article IV, Section 5(c) shall not be passed on or as an emergency?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Independence A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Sections 2(a) and 2(b) of the Charter of the City of Independence be amended to provide that the position of the Finance Director transition from an elected office to a position appointed by the Mayor, effective January 1, 2028, subject to confirmation by at least five (5) members of Council and serving until he or she resigns, dies, or is removed by at least five (5) members of Council; and provide that a Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college or university and have at least five years of experience in government accounting or public finance be required?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Lakewood A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Section 2.2 of the Third Amended Charter of the City of Lakewood be amended to require that prior to making an appointment to a vacancy in Council, remaining members of Council shall first issue an open call for all interested candidates to submit applications and, upon Council's review of the applications, shall hold candidate interviews in public session?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Lakewood A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Section 2.8 of the Third Amended Charter of the City of Lakewood be amended to allow the revision, repeal, or amendment of an ordinance or resolution by underlining inserted language and striking through language that is being removed?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Lakewood A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Section 6.7 of the Third Amended Charter of the City of Lakewood be amended to provide that on or before March 1 of each odd numbered year, the Civil Service Commission shall set forth the commission's recommendations for the salary and other compensation for the offices of mayor and members of council?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Lakewood A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Section 7.5 of the Third Amended Charter of the City of Lakewood be amended to clarify that amendments to the Charter may be submitted to the registered voters of the city in three manners: upon the recommendation of a two-thirds majority vote of the members of the Charter Review Commission and submission by Council to a vote of the people; by an affirmative vote of Council of at least two-thirds of councilmembers; or upon receipt of a petition signed by not less than ten percent (10%) of the registered voters of the city?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Lakewood A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall the Third Amended Charter of the City of Lakewood be amended by adding new Section 7.2 (i) to require that, commencing with the Federal decennial census of 2030, the Planning Commission shall review and make, if necessary, appropriate redivisions of the City into four wards, which shall be as nearly equal in population as possible, and composed of contiguous and compact territory, bounded by natural boundaries or street lines; and that any changes made in ward boundaries shall become effective for the next regular municipal election?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Maple Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article III, Section 1 of the Charter of the City of Maple Heights be amended to provide that each member of Council shall have resided continuously in the City for a period of at least two (2) years preceding their election; and that they shall have resided continually in the district from which the Councilperson seeks election, for a period of at least two (2) years preceding their election?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Maple Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article III, Section 3 of the Charter of the City of Maple Heights be amended to delete the provision that an elective officer who is absent from the duties of office for three months, or disqualified from office, may continue in office until a successor is qualified?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Maple Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VII, Section 12 of the Charter of the City of Maple Heights be amended to permit ordinances or resolutions embracing the subjects of salaries, the necessity for and intention to install public improvements which contain provisions for assessments against abutting properties, or grants of public utility franchises, be posted on the City’s website and social media accounts and in four (4) public places in the City, said places determined by Council?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Maple Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XIII, Section 7 of the Charter of the City of Maple Heights be amended to correct a grammatical error by revising the phrase “committee of the petitions” to “committee of the petitioners?”

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Maple Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XX, Section 2 of the Charter of the City of Maple Heights be amended to provide that, beginning in January 2031 and each five (5) years thereafter, the Mayor, the Council President, and each member of Council, from within their District, shall appoint one qualified elector of the City and respective District, holding no other office or appointment with the City of Maple Heights, as members of a nine (9) person Charter Review Commission; that the Mayor and President of Council shall appoint one (1) alternate member each, to serve if a Commission member(s) is absent for a meeting; and if a Commission member(s) is absent for a meeting, then one, or both of the alternates, as necessary, may be appointed by a majority of the members present for the meeting to replace the absent member for that meeting only, with all the same rights and duties as the absent member; and to provide for the election of a Chairperson pro tem from among the Commission members?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Olmsted Falls A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article III, Section 3.01 of the Charter of the City of Olmsted Falls be amended to provide that the Municipality shall have all powers, without limitation, of local self-government and municipal home rule; that no law of the State of Ohio or of the United States shall be imposed upon the city except where mandated by law, unless the city adopts or approves such state or federal law by this Charter or legislative act; that this Charter and city ordinances, rules and regulations shall be construed broadly in favor of the home rule power of the city where possible; and that none of the powers herein shall be withdrawn from the exclusive control of the city, nor shall the corporate existence of the city terminate or merge, nor shall any territory be detached from or annexed to the city without approval of the council and as specified in this Charter?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Olmsted Falls A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article V, Section 5.03(c) of the Charter of the City of Olmsted Falls be amended to provide that monetary contracts involving amounts less than the dollar limit set for department heads in the purchasing approval section of the city’s codified ordinances must be reviewed and approved by the law department prior to their execution and shall be entered into and enforced by the Mayor; and that all other contracts require the authority of council for their execution and shall be entered into and enforced by the Mayor?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Olmsted Falls A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article V, Section 5.08 of the Charter of the City of Olmsted Falls be amended to provide that Council may adopt an emergency ordinance or resolution for the efficient operation of the municipality?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Olmsted Falls A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VII, Section 7.08 of the Charter of the City of Olmsted Falls be amended by extending the timeframe for holding a recall election from not fewer than forty (40) days and no more than fifty-five (55) days from the date of the certification of sufficiency of a petition demanding the recall and removal of an elected officer, to not fewer than sixty (60) days and no more than ninety (90) days from the date of the certification of sufficiency of said petition?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Olmsted Falls A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VIII, Section 8.02 of the Charter of the City of Olmsted Falls be amended to provide that the Director of Finance shall have no less than six (6) years of accounting experience, preferably with at least three (3) such years working in municipal government accounting; and remove the requirement that the Director of Finance shall have at least three (3) years’ experience in municipal government accounting?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article II, Section 1 of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended to provide for a change in the term for Mayor from two (2) to four (4) years; and that beginning with the 2027 municipal election, the Mayor shall be elected every fourth year thereafter for a term of four (4) years?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article II, Section 3 of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended to provide that Council may, by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the members of Council after public hearing, expel or remove the Mayor from office for gross misconduct, malfeasance, nonfeasance, misfeasance in or disqualification for office; for violation of the Mayor’s oath of office; for conviction while in office of a crime involving moral turpitude; for absence without justifiable excuse from three consecutive regular Council meetings; or for mental or physical disability rendering it impossible for the Mayor to perform the duties of Mayor?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article III, Section 2 of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended to provide for a change in terms of all Members of Council from two (2) to four (4) year terms; that beginning with the 2027 municipal election, Ward council members shall be elected every fourth year for a four (4) year term; and beginning with the 2029 municipal election, At-Large council members shall be elected every fourth year for a four (4) year term?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Section 2 (A) of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended to change the term of the Director of Law from two (2) to four (4) years by providing that beginning with the 2027 municipal election, the Director of Law shall be elected every fourth year thereafter for a term of four (4) years?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IV, Section 2 (B) of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended to provide that Council may, by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the members of Council after public hearing, expel or remove the Director of Law from office for gross misconduct, malfeasance, nonfeasance, misfeasance in or disqualification for office; for violation of their oath of office; for conviction while in office of a crime involving moral turpitude; or for mental or physical disability rendering it impossible for them to perform the duties of the Director of Law?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article IX of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended by amending Sections 1, 2, and 3, and eliminating sections 4 and 5, to provide that beginning in 2027, all municipal elections shall be non-partisan elections; that the names of two (2) persons receiving the highest number of votes in the primary election held in September for each office shall be nominated to be candidates for the offices of mayor, law director and ward councilman at the next succeeding regular municipal elections; for candidates for the offices of at-large councilmen, the names of five (5) persons receiving the highest number of votes shall be nominated at the next succeeding regular municipal elections; and to provide that a petition shall require signatures of registered electors of not less than fifty (50) for ward councilman, and one hundred fifty (150) for councilman- at-large, mayor, and law director?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Rocky River A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VIII, Section 2 of the Charter of the City of Rocky River be amended to provide that within twenty (20) days of the filing of a recall petition, the Clerk, in consultation with the Board of Elections, shall determine whether or not it meets the requirements to hold a recall election; and to expand the timeframe for holding a recall election from between thirty (30) and forty-five (45) days, to not less than sixty (60) and no more than seventy-five (75) days after the delivery of notice to the elected officer of a sufficient petition calling for the officer to resign?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Seven Hills A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article V, Section 8 (d) of the Charter of the City of Seven Hills be amended to provide that the determination of the Zoning Board of Appeals on any variance request shall be deemed final and shall not require further approval by any other municipal body, and subject only to judicial appeal as permitted under State Law (Ohio Revised Code Section 713.11)?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Solon A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VI, Section 10.A of the Charter of the City of Solon be amended to provide that on or before January of 2029 the Director of Planning and Community Development with the assistance of the Master Plan Citizen’s Committee, shall commence a comprehensive review of the City of Solon Master Plan; and to add subsection (d) to provide the Planning Department and Economic Development Department shall jointly provide biannual reports to City leadership and relevant stakeholders detailing a summary of key accomplishments, including notable project completions and measurable wins, clear identification of risks, constraints or challenges, an outlook of anticipated projects, opportunities and priorities, as well as a detailed summary of required resources necessary to successfully execute identified initiatives?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Solon A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XIV of the Charter of the City of Solon be amended to add Section 5 to provide that Council shall adopt a procedure and process for the Zoning and Development of the Industrial Core Area as identified and described within the City of Solon Master Plan, which shall not employ the procedure and process contained in Sections 1 and 2 in Article XIV, which requires that any ordinance effecting a change in the zoning classification, zoning map change, or zoning use shall be approved by a majority of electors voting thereon?

Proposed Charter Amendment City of Solon A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XIV, Sections 1 and 2 of the Charter of the City of Solon be amended to repeal the requirement that any zoning district change or zoning use change be approved by a majority of the electors in each ward in which a change in zoning classification, zoning district, or zoning use change of any property is located?

Proposed Charter Amendment County of Cuyahoga A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article II, Section 2.03 and Article VI, Section 6.04 of the Charter of the County of Cuyahoga be amended to require that County Council confirm the County Executive’s removal of members of boards, agencies, commissions and authorities as are or may hereafter be created by or pursuant to the Charter, as are provided by general law to be appointed by boards of county commissioners, and on special boards and commissions created by any agreement with another public agency or court order?

Proposed Charter Amendment County of Cuyahoga A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article V, Section 5.06 of the Charter of the County of Cuyahoga be amended to provide that the Director of Law shall provide primary legal representation on labor negotiations, grievances and arbitrations, non- litigation related employment matters, public records matters, risk management functions and activities, and non-litigation related contracts, agreements, debt issuance documents, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, and other legal instruments entered into by the County Executive on behalf of Cuyahoga County; that the powers and duties of the Director of Law shall include giving written opinions and other legal advice to the Executive, County Council, officers, departments, directors, boards, agencies, commissions, and authorities appointed or established under the various Articles of the Charter, and other County entities whose chief executive officers serve at the pleasure of the County Executive or County Council; that nothing prohibits the County Executive, County Council or other entities established by Charter, Council, or general law, from seeking or obtaining advice from the Prosecuting Attorney; that this Section 5.06 shall not in any way limit the powers and duties of the Prosecuting Attorney as set forth in Section 4.01 and general law; and that in no event shall the Director of Law prosecute, defend, appear in court, or otherwise handle any action in any litigation or litigation-related proceedings on behalf of the County or any of its entities, unless referred to the Law Director by the Prosecuting Attorney?

Proposed Charter Amendment County of Cuyahoga A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article XII, Section 12.09 of the Charter of the County of Cuyahoga be amended to provide that four (4) members of the Charter Review Commission shall be appointed by the County Executive, and such appointments shall not be subject to Council confirmation; four (4) members shall be appointed by the Council, and such appointments shall not be presented to the County Executive for approval or disapproval; and that one (1) member shall be appointed by the County Executive, subject to confirmation by Council?

Proposed Charter Amendment Village of Brooklyn Heights A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage.
